title: prompt-priming-delay-stabilization
creator: Nisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers (hosted + Dedicated tenants + Private demo) reported a reproducible regression in first-token latency (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec for some LLM variants when requests included long prompt priming (system + few-shot examples). The increase manifests as a 120–400ms TTFT delta and 20–35% tokens/sec drop for affected quantized/int8 model variants on GPU pools with heterogeneous NUMA configs.

Symptoms / Observables:
- Elevated TTFT on initial stream burst following priming sequences >2k tokens; subsequent tokens stabilize but overall throughput lower.
- Spike in request queue time and worker-side prefetch handshake retries visible in runtime traces.
- Kernel selection logs show repeated kernel-mismatch fallback for ~15% of requests (int8 kernels selected then fallback to slower path).
- CPU-side thread contention (NUMA imbalance) correlates with higher variance in emitter loop latency.

Reproduction steps (internal):
1) Use model rwd-open-7b-int8-stride with prompt containing 2k token priming (3-shot).
2) Send 50 concurrent short-completion requests (max_tokens=64) across multiplexed connections.
3) Observe TTFT histogram; tail shifts at 95th/99th.
4) Enable tracing and KV prefetch debug to capture handshake failure rate.

Initial root-cause hypothesis:
- Recent prefetch handshake change (prefetch backoff) introduced a timing window where KV cache warmup attempts are retried under heavy priming, creating micro-backpressure into the multiplexer.
- For certain stride/seq_len combos the kernel selector heuristic mispredicts optimal int8 kernel causeing fallback and additional kernel load latency.
- Combined effect: more scheduling jitter + fallback penalties => TTFT and tokens/sec regression.

Proposed mitigation (short-term):
- Revert prefetch backoff heuristics to last-known-stable parameters for affected runtime path and add conservative jitter to retry interval.
- Add a compatibility guard in kernel-selector: if fallback rate > 5% within 30s window, prefer slower-but-stable kernel to avoid repeated back-and-forth penalty.
- Introduce a temporary per-tenant priming-safe-path flag that forces synchronous KV warmup for the first request after large priming (used for Dedicated/Private escalations).

Proposed long-term plan:
- Implement adaptive kernel-reliability scoring (persist per-model kernel success rates) and surface to optimizer UI in Console.
- Extend prefetch diagnostics and add autopilot tuning to avoid oscillatory backoff.
- Add NUMA-aware worker placement check for Dedicated/Private nodes to reduce emitter-thread contention.

Rollout plan:
- Patch branch created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12345
- Canary: 5% of hosted traffic for rwd-open-7b-int8-stride in region us-west1, and 2 Dedicated tenants that escalated.
- Monitor TTFT (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, kernel-fallback-rate, prefetch-retry-rate for 48h.
- If stable for 48h, ramp to 25% then full.
- Rollback criteria: TTFT p95 increases by >15% vs baseline or customer errors spike >1.5x.

Monitoring & Dashboards:
- Dashboard: /dashboards/priming-latency-2026 (internal)
- Alert thresholds: TTFT p95 > 350ms for rwd-open-7b-int8-stride; kernel-fallback-rate > 7% for 10m window.

Stakeholders & Communication:
- Escalation owners: Emily Chen (SRE), Rajesh Singh (Support), Marco Alvarez (Runtime Eng).
- Notifying customers via SOC portal and direct slack threads (channels: #cust-escalations, #dedicated-ops).

Notes: This ticket focuses only on stabilizing the production regression and putting conservative fallbacks in place. Follow-ups will track performance optimization and persistent kernel-selection improvements.
